topic: Public explainer on physical activity for generally healthy adults
scope: Public education example; it does not diagnose disease or give personal training or medication plans. The summaries are paraphrased by the project authors.

W1.title: WHO: Physical activity (WHO/Europe fact sheet)
W1.summary: Adults should do 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity a week, or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, or an equivalent combination, plus muscle-strengthening activities involving the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week. Doing some activity is better than doing none, and people can start with small amounts and increase gradually.
W1.locator: Recommended amounts for adults are on the WHO/Europe page; starting small and increasing gradually is in the ADULTS good practice statements of the executive summary of the WHO 2020 guidelines (on NCBI Bookshelf).

W2.title: WHO: Physical activity
W2.summary: Activity is not limited to exercise; it also includes walking, cycling and physical activity in daily life. Regular activity benefits physical and mental health, and sedentary time should be reduced. All kinds of activity count, but not every light movement can be equated with meeting the moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic target.
W2.locator: Overview; How much physical activity is recommended?

editorial_boundaries: This restates the material for generally healthy adults; children, pregnancy and postpartum, chronic conditions and rehabilitation each need their own context.
General examples such as walking to work or breaking up long periods of sitting may be used; do not set an intensity for a particular reader or claim treatment effects.
The text must not add medication doses, advice to stop medication, or diagnostic judgments.
